text: It starts in the throat. Tiny muscles in the voice box twitch many times a second, as the cat breathes in and out.
Kittens start purring when they're just a few days old, while nursing with their mom.
But purring isn't only about happiness. Cats also purr when they're scared, hurt, or giving birth.
Some scientists think the low vibrations might even help bones and tissue heal.
And some cats have a trick: a hungry purr with a hidden cry inside, that people find hard to ignore.
So when your cat purrs at breakfast... is it love, or is it food?
